provenance: 64 individually hand-authored synthetic tape-library tickets across eight families, 2026-10-21. Text only trains the baseline; telemetry and labels support corpus review. No held-out file is read by the corpus authoring script. Same AI author as heldout; no external validation claimed.

cases.title: Restore job stuck at mount
cases.text: A restore job asked the library to mount a cartridge and waited for minutes. The robot picked the tape but the drive load did not finish before the backup software gave up.

cases.title: Load request exceeds timeout
cases.text: The mtx load command for drive 2 hung well past the usual time. The changer reported the move as complete, yet the drive stayed not ready while the mount timer ran out.

cases.title: Mount queue waits on one drive
cases.text: Several mount requests are queued behind one drive that takes too long to become ready after each cartridge load. Load wait seconds keep climbing on that drive only.

cases.title: Slow cartridge load after move
cases.text: After the robot moved the cartridge from its slot, the drive reported becoming ready for a long time. The mount request timed out and the job was rescheduled.

cases.title: Backup window missed on mount
cases.text: Nightly backup missed its window because each tape mount took several minutes. The library accepted every move command, but drive load and thread time stayed very slow.

cases.title: Load timeout on archive drive
cases.text: An archive copy waited on a tape load that never completed. sg_turs kept returning not ready, becoming ready, while the mount request sat at the timeout limit.

cases.title: Drive slow to thread tape
cases.text: The drive takes a long time to thread a newly loaded cartridge. Mount latency exceeds the timeout and the application logs a load timeout for the requested volume.

cases.title: Robot move done, mount pending
cases.text: The changer finished moving the cartridge into the drive but the mount request is still pending. Load wait time crossed two minutes and the job reported a mount timeout.

cases.title: Drive asks for cleaning
cases.text: sg_logs page 0x2e shows TapeAlert flag 20 Clean now on drive 1. The drive keeps running jobs but asks for a cleaning cartridge before more writes.

cases.title: Periodic cleaning flag set
cases.text: TapeAlert flag 21 Clean periodic is set on drive 3. The cleaning schedule has lapsed and the drive requests routine head cleaning.

cases.title: Clean now after long write
cases.text: After a long write session the drive raised the clean now TapeAlert flag. Read retries rose slightly and the drive requests a cleaning cartridge.

cases.title: Both cleaning flags present
cases.text: TapeAlert page shows both clean now and clean periodic flags on the same drive. No cleaning cartridge has been loaded into this drive for weeks.

cases.title: Cleaning request in sense data
cases.text: Request sense returns cleaning requested on drive 4 and the TapeAlert log page lists flag 20. The heads may need cleaning before the next backup.

cases.title: Library reports drive needs cleaning
cases.text: The library front panel says drive 2 needs cleaning, and sg_logs on the drive confirms the TapeAlert clean now flag. Auto clean is disabled in this lab.

cases.title: Cleaning cartridge expected
cases.text: Operators see a cleaning request from drive 5 every morning. The TapeAlert clean flag is set again and the cleaning cartridge slot is still occupied.

cases.title: Head cleaning overdue
cases.text: Drive 6 reports head cleaning overdue through TapeAlert clean periodic. Write performance is normal, but the cleaning flag must be handled before heavy jobs.

cases.title: LTFS volume will not mount
cases.text: ltfs refuses to mount the volume and reports an index inconsistency between the index partition and the data partition. The volume was unloaded during a power cut.

cases.title: Index generation mismatch
cases.text: The LTFS index on partition a is older than the index on partition b. Mount fails with an inconsistent index error and suggests running ltfsck.

cases.title: ltfsck reports index problem
cases.text: ltfsck reports that the latest index on the data partition cannot be read cleanly. Rollback points are listed but nobody has chosen one yet.

cases.title: LTFS mount after crash
cases.text: After a host crash the LTFS volume shows index errors on mount. The file system was writing when the crash happened, so the last index was not committed.

cases.title: Damaged LTFS index
cases.text: The LTFS volume reports a damaged index and mounts read only at best. Index errors appear for the most recent generation on the data partition.

cases.title: Unexpected end of LTFS index
cases.text: LTFS logs an unexpected end of index while mounting the cartridge. The index partition holds an older generation than the data partition.

cases.title: LTFS consistency check needed
cases.text: The LTFS mount helper asks for a consistency check. Two index generations disagree and the volume cannot be mounted for writing.

cases.title: LTFS rollback question
cases.text: An LTFS cartridge fails to mount after an interrupted write. ltfsck lists several rollback points, and an index error count is recorded for the newest one.

cases.title: Repeated bus resets on tape path
cases.text: The kernel log shows repeated unit attention, power on or reset occurred, for the tape drive. Jobs fail mid-write after each SCSI bus reset.

cases.title: Unit attentions after cable work
cases.text: Since cable work on the tape path, the drive returns unit attention sense 06/29/00 several times an hour. lsscsi shows the device dropping and returning.

cases.title: Device renumbered after reset
cases.text: The drive keeps resetting and reappears with a new /dev/sg number. Unit attention reports power on reset each time the SCSI path recovers.

cases.title: HBA link flaps
cases.text: The HBA reports link resets toward the tape drive. Each reset produces a unit attention and the running backup aborts.

cases.title: Medium may have changed alerts
cases.text: The drive returns unit attention 06/28/00 medium may have changed and 06/29/00 reset without anyone touching the library. The path seems unstable.

cases.title: Tape path resets during backup
cases.text: During backups the SCSI transport resets the tape target repeatedly. Every reset generates a unit attention that the application treats as a failure.

cases.title: Zoning change and resets
cases.text: After a zoning change, the tape drive logs repeated unit attentions and target resets. sg_inq still returns the right serial between resets.

cases.title: Unstable SCSI path to drive
cases.text: The SCSI path to drive 3 is unstable. Unit attention counts climb through the day and lsscsi shows the device briefly missing.

cases.title: Drive reports hardware error
cases.text: sg_logs page 0x2e shows TapeAlert flag 30 Hardware A on drive 2. Request sense returns a hardware error sense key and the drive stops accepting jobs.

cases.title: Hardware B flag on drive
cases.text: TapeAlert flag 31 Hardware B is set and the drive failed its power-on self test. The library marks the drive as failed.

cases.title: Internal target failure
cases.text: The drive returns sense key 4 hardware error with ASC 44 internal target failure. TapeAlert hardware flags are set on the log page.

cases.title: Drive fault light on
cases.text: The drive fault indicator is on and TapeAlert reports a hardware fault flag. The firmware log records an internal drive error.

cases.title: Drive hardware failure mid job
cases.text: A write job aborted with a hardware error. The TapeAlert page lists flags 30 and 31 together and the drive needs a vendor diagnostic.

cases.title: Hardware error after firmware load
cases.text: After a firmware load the drive reports hardware error sense data and TapeAlert hardware A. Test unit ready fails with a hardware sense key.

cases.title: Drive mechanism fault
cases.text: The drive mechanism reports a fault while loading and TapeAlert sets the hardware flag. The cartridge is ejected and the drive goes offline.

cases.title: Drive self test failure
cases.text: The drive self test fails with a hardware error and TapeAlert hardware B is set. Jobs routed to this drive fail immediately.

cases.title: Barcode missing from inventory
cases.text: mtx status no longer lists a barcode that the backup catalog expects in slot 14. The library inventory disagrees with the expected list.

cases.title: Slot shows wrong barcode
cases.text: The library reports a different barcode in slot 7 than the catalog. Inventory mismatch appears after someone opened the library door.

cases.title: Element status disagrees
cases.text: mtx status shows a full data transfer element while the catalog says the cartridge is home in its storage slot. Several elements disagree.

cases.title: Inventory changed after door open
cases.text: After the library door was opened, the element status changed for several slots. Barcodes no longer match the expected inventory list.

cases.title: Import export slot confusion
cases.text: A cartridge placed in the import export slot never appeared in a storage slot. The inventory shows an unknown barcode and one missing volume.

cases.title: Duplicate barcode in library
cases.text: The library inventory lists the same barcode in two slots. The catalog expects one cartridge, so the inventory disagrees.

cases.title: Library lost track of tape
cases.text: The library cannot find a cartridge the catalog expects. mtx status shows the slot empty and the inventory mismatch count rises.

cases.title: Stale inventory after power loss
cases.text: After a power loss the library reports a stale inventory. Barcodes in several slots differ from the expected list until a rescan is approved.

cases.title: Cartridge flagged by drive
cases.text: TapeAlert flag 4 Media is set after reading cartridge LTO tape A00123. The drive suggests the cartridge may be damaged.

cases.title: Media life warning
cases.text: TapeAlert flag 7 Media life is set on a cartridge with a very high load count. sg_read_attr shows the cartridge has been loaded thousands of times.

cases.title: Unrecovered read on one cartridge
cases.text: Reads fail with medium error 03/11/00 unrecovered read error on one cartridge only. TapeAlert media flags are set and other cartridges read fine.

cases.title: Suspect tape after drop
cases.text: A cartridge was dropped during handling. The drive now raises the media TapeAlert flag and read retries spike on that tape.

cases.title: Media error on restore
cases.text: A restore fails with a medium error and TapeAlert flag 4. The cartridge memory shows the tape is near the end of its rated life.

cases.title: Worn cartridge
cases.text: The cartridge is old and worn. The drive reports the media life TapeAlert flag and the MAM attributes show heavy use.

cases.title: Media flag follows cartridge
cases.text: The media TapeAlert flag appears whenever this cartridge is loaded, in any drive. The cartridge barcode is the common factor.

cases.title: Damaged cartridge leader
cases.text: The drive reports a medium error and the media TapeAlert flag after loading a cartridge with a suspected leader problem.

cases.title: Writes rejected write protected
cases.text: Every write to the cartridge fails with DATA PROTECT sense 07/27/00 write protected. The backup job aborts at the first block.

cases.title: WORM cartridge rejects append
cases.text: A WORM cartridge rejects an overwrite and the drive returns data protect sense. The application tried to reuse a write once volume.

cases.title: Write protect tab set
cases.text: mt status shows WR_PROT for the loaded cartridge. The write protect tab on the cartridge is set and writes are rejected.

cases.title: Archive tape is read only
cases.text: An archive cartridge was loaded for a scratch write. The drive reports write protected and refuses the write.

cases.title: Data protect on label write
cases.text: Labeling a new cartridge fails with data protect, write protected. The operator is unsure whether the tab is set.

cases.title: Scratch pool contains protected tape
cases.text: A scratch pool cartridge rejects writes with write protected sense. The tape was moved into scratch by mistake.

cases.title: Write protect rejections climb
cases.text: Write protect rejections climb as jobs try the same cartridge again and again. mt status reports WR_PROT on each load.

cases.title: Cannot overwrite volume
cases.text: The backup software cannot overwrite an expired volume. The drive reports the cartridge as write protected with sense key 7.
